title: Console API: add scaling policy endpoints (read/update) w/ RBAC + validation
author: Chloe Martin
description: Summary: Exposes Dedicated deployment scaling policy to the Console via new control-plane endpoints for reading/updating per-deployment scaling policy, including RBAC enforcement and input validation. This unblocks the Console settings page and the internal admin tooling to toggle bounded scaling + predictive mode behind flags. Context: Dedicated autoscaling bounds + predictive mode initiative requires customer-configurable min/max and related settings; schema + migrations are in earlier PRs, this PR focuses on the HTTP surface area + authn/authz + validation semantics. Endpoints: (1) GET /v1/console/dedicated/deployments/{deployment_id}/scaling-policy -> returns effective policy + source (explicit vs default) + feature availability; (2) PUT /v1/console/dedicated/deployments/{deployment_id}/scaling-policy -> updates explicit policy for that deployment; (3) POST /v1/console/dedicated/deployments/{deployment_id}/scaling-policy:validate -> dry-run validation to support UI preflight and better inline errors. RBAC: Requires console user to have dedicated.deployment.read for GET and dedicated.deployment.write for PUT; write also requires account-level permission dedicated.scaling_policy.write (new permission gate) to keep rollout safe during pilot. RBAC is enforced server-side with consistent denial responses (403 + error_code=INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS) and is wired to existing Console auth context. Validation: Validates min_replicas/max_replicas bounds, cooldown durations, and predictive mode toggles; rejects min > max; rejects negative values; enforces upper caps on max_replicas based on contract quota (if present) with a clear error message (error_code=EXCEEDS_ACCOUNT_QUOTA). Predictive mode validation checks feature flag availability and blocks enablement if the account isn’t allowlisted. Also adds request rate-limiting for policy updates (basic per-deployment throttle) to prevent config churn from misbehaving clients; returns 429 with retry_after_seconds when throttled. Semantics: PUT is idempotent with full replacement of the explicit policy block; fields omitted in the payload are treated as “unset” and will revert to defaults (UI will typically send the full form state). Response includes both the stored explicit policy and the computed effective policy after defaults + bounds clamping rules (as defined in ADR). Auditability: This PR adds structured logs for reads/writes with request_id, actor_id, account_id, deployment_id, and policy_hash. It does not emit the final audit-log events for compliance (that’s in ENG-22146 / PR-48235), but it does plumb actor metadata through so audit events can be emitted in the shared middleware later. Testing: Added unit tests for validators, RBAC guards, and quota checks; added integration tests for the Console API router verifying 403/404/422 behavior. Manual testing: verified from Console dev environment using curl and the admin impersonation tool; verified the UI can render validation errors without leaking internal fields. Rollout: Endpoints are deployed but write-path is effectively gated by dedicated.scaling_policy.write permission + account feature flag; safe for general release while pilot is in progress. Follow-ups: Console UI form wiring in ENG-22144; audit event emission in ENG-22146; documentation and Terraform support tracked separately.
commits: console-api: add scaling policy routes + handlers
validation: enforce min/max invariants + cooldown bounds
quota: clamp/deny max_replicas above contracted quota
tests: add router integration tests for scaling policy endpoints
logging: add structured logs w/ actor + deployment context
notable_snippets: PUT response includes: explicit_policy, effective_policy, warnings[] (e.g. "predictive requested but disabled; falling back to reactive"), and validation_errors[] when called via :validate.
Validation errors are stable for Console: {field, message, error_code}. Example error_code: MIN_GREATER_THAN_MAX, INVALID_COOLDOWN, FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED.
review_conversation: 2025-06-25 Ethan Park: Can we make sure PUT is fully idempotent and doesn’t merge partial payloads? Console tends to resend full state but other clients may not. Also, please confirm defaulting semantics when a field is omitted vs set to null.

2025-06-25 Chloe Martin (author): Good call. Updated controller to treat omitted fields as unset (revert to defaults) and reject explicit nulls for scalar fields (422) to keep semantics crisp. Added tests for omitted vs provided fields.

2025-06-26 Benji Okafor: Validation: please align error_code values with the pattern we use in other Console APIs (SCREAMING_SNAKE). Also, we should return 404 for deployments not found instead of 403 to avoid resource enumeration—what’s our precedent?

2025-06-26 Chloe Martin (author): Updated error_code casing. For 403 vs 404: followed existing dedicated deployment endpoints (RBAC check first, then 404). Added a note to the security section in the description; happy to change if we want consistent non-enumeration behavior.
2025-06-26 Marcus Lin: Prefer non-enumeration. If the caller lacks read permission, return 404 regardless of existence. Same for write. Can we adjust the middleware ordering?

2025-06-27 Chloe Martin (author): Adjusted ordering: resolve deployment under a scoped query by account first; if not found, 404. RBAC is evaluated after we have the account/deployment context but before returning details; for insufficient perms we now return 404 with error_code=NOT_FOUND. Added tests covering both cases.

2025-06-27 Felix Schneider: Can we include effective_policy in GET? The UI needs to display what’s actually in force (esp. defaults + gating). Also include warnings when predictive is requested but blocked.
2025-06-27 Chloe Martin (author): Added effective_policy + warnings to GET, and also to PUT response for immediate UI feedback.

2025-06-28 Tessa Morgan: UX-related: please ensure validation error messages are user-readable (no internal jargon like "quota_enforcer"). Also make sure cooldown units are explicit (seconds) in schema.
2025-06-28 Chloe Martin (author): Updated messages; OpenAPI now specifies durations in seconds and the response field names match. Pushed final changes.
2025-06-28 Ethan Park: Looks good. Please add a short note in OpenAPI about feature gating behavior for predictive fields (422 vs warning).
2025-06-28 Marcus Lin: Approved (with the 404 non-enumeration change).
release_notes: Internal: Console can now read/update Dedicated scaling policy via control-plane endpoints (gated by permissions/feature flags).
No customer-visible change unless account is allowlisted for scaling policy writes.
